answer:
Based on the analysis performed, here are the results:

## Incident Counts and Rates per Zone

I spatially joined the 256 incidents to the 9 zones (251 matched, 5 fell outside all zones) and computed the rate per 1,000 residents using each zone's population field.

| Zone | Population | Incidents | Rate per 1,000 |
|------|-----------|-----------|----------------|
| Z1 | 5,200 | 41 | 7.88 |
| **Z2** | **830** | **19** | **22.89** |
| Z3 | 4,100 | 22 | 5.37 |
| Z4 | 2,600 | 18 | 6.92 |
| Z5 | 7,400 | 66 | 8.92 |
| Z6 | 3,900 | 25 | 6.41 |
| Z7 | 1,500 | 9 | 6.00 |
| Z8 | 6,100 | 37 | 6.07 |
| Z9 | 2,800 | 14 | 5.00 |

## Answer

**Zone Z2 has the highest rate: 22.89 incidents per 1,000 residents** (19 incidents against a population of just 830). This is by far the highest — more than 2.5× the next-highest zone (Z5 at 8.92 per 1,000), driven by its very small population relative to its incident count.

**Artifacts produced:**
- **Interactive choropleth map** of incidents per zone: [incidents_per_zone.geojson](https://agent/files/file_47f0d43291db/download) (on your map, shaded by `point_count`)
- **Results table**: [zone_incident_rates.csv](https://agent/files/file_02520902ea5b/download)

Note: 5 of the 256 incidents fell outside all 9 zone polygons and were excluded from the counts.
